solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Grab a customer blocking counter (6)

indicators.note: the answer sits as one block across the words before it

annotation.surface: A shop assistant is told to seize a shopper standing in the way of the till.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Counter' looks like a shop counter, and 'Grab' like an order; in fact the counter is a bead frame for counting.
annotation.definitionFit: An abacus is a counting frame, something you count on.

entries.clue: Newly-wed thriving in prison (9)

annotation.surface: A happy new spouse turns out to be flourishing behind bars.
annotation.walkthrough: Bridewell was a London prison, and its name became a general word for a house of correction.
annotation.definitionFit: A bridewell is an old word for a jail, after the London prison of that name.

entries.clue: Arm of TUC upset group ignored by leader of Conservatives (7)

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned upside down is read bottom to top
the C is left out, disregarded

blocks.clueFragment: group ignored by leader of Conservatives

annotation.surface: A wing of the Trades Union Congress is annoyed at being snubbed by the Tory leader.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Arm' reads as a branch of an organisation; it is a weapon. The TUC is Britain's Trades Union Congress.
annotation.definitionFit: A cutlass is a short curved sword, a weapon or arm.

entries.clue: Idiot’s backward step (3)

indicators.note: the word is written the other way round

blocks.note: a pas is a step in ballet

annotation.surface: Going backwards is a fool's move.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Backward step' reads as a regression; in fact 'backward' works on the dance step PAS.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a sap is a gullible, easily fooled person, someone the sap of a tree makes soft and wet.

entries.clue: Constituent briefly a fan of substantial backing (8)

indicators.note: cut short by its last letter
backing is moving in reverse, so the word is read from its end

blocks.note: INTO (a fan of) without its last letter

annotation.surface: A voter who is a keen supporter of a big financial backer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Constituent' looks like a noun for a voter; here it is the adjective, as in a constituent part. Being 'into' something means being a fan of it.
annotation.definitionFit: An integral part is a constituent one, forming part of the whole.

entries.clue: River pilot going out of business (5)

indicators.note: the pilot leaves the longer word

blocks.note: to pilot a scheme is to try it out; removed

annotation.surface: A river pilot quits his trade.
annotation.walkthrough: 'River pilot' reads as one person who steers boats; the words split, with 'River' the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the Indus flows from Tibet through Pakistan to the Arabian Sea, and gave India its name.

entries.clue: Upfront dad with gender dysphoria? (11)

annotation.surface: A father who is open about being transgender.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: a trans parent is a father with gender dysphoria, and 'transparent' means open and honest.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone upfront is transparent, hiding nothing.

entries.clue: Enterprising Indian chief (2-5)

annotation.surface: A bold, ambitious tribal leader.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Indian chief' suggests a Native American leader; it is the head of Goa, a state in India.
annotation.definitionFit: A go-ahead person or firm is enterprising and ambitious.

entries.clue: Sign of one in thrall to warmonger (5)

indicators.note: held inside, as a captive

blocks.note: Ares, the Greek god of war

annotation.surface: A sign that someone is under the spell of a hawkish leader.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sign' reads as a symptom; it is a star sign. ARES holds I.
annotation.definitionFit: Aries, the Ram, is the first sign of the zodiac.

entries.clue: Hapless MP edits last of Trotsky’s letters arranged in wrong order (8)

annotation.definitionNote: a description of the letters, matching the participle MISTYPED

indicators.note: unlucky, knocked about, so the letters are rearranged
the last of anything is its final part, here the closing letter of a word

annotation.surface: A luckless politician is editing Trotsky's correspondence and muddles it.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue is fairly &lit-flavoured: shuffling letters is both what the solver does and what a typo is. 'Letters' reads as correspondence; here it is characters on a keyboard.
annotation.definitionFit: A typing slip such as a transposition puts characters out of sequence on the keyboard, so the text is mistyped.

entries.clue: Soldiers entertained by American writer’s language (6)

indicators.note: a host holds its guests inside

annotation.surface: Troops are hosted by a US author, who speaks their tongue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'American writer' suggests a novelist; it splits into A and BIC, the ballpoint pen.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Arabic is the tongue spoken across North Africa and the Middle East, one language among many.

entries.clue: Bones chanced upon west of a Turkish city (10)

indicators.note: in an across clue, west is to the left, so it comes first

blocks.note: Tarsus, in southern Turkey, birthplace of St Paul

annotation.surface: Remains were stumbled upon to the west of a city in Turkey.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface reads like an archaeological find, and the bones are those of the foot.
annotation.definitionFit: The metatarsus is the group of five bones in the foot.

entries.clue: Somehow dreading son’s mess (1,4,6)

indicators.note: in some way or other, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: In some way fearing the chaos a son will make.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mess' reads as the son's untidiness; it is also a meal, which fits the dinner in the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A dog's dinner is British slang for a complete mess.

entries.clue: Partner’s celebration starting late (4)

indicators.note: the word begins after its first letter

annotation.surface: A spouse's party got going behind schedule.
annotation.walkthrough: In bridge, East and West are partners, so either can be 'Partner'.
annotation.definitionFit: East is West's partner at the bridge table.

entries.clue: Reportedly think cat does this (4)

indicators.note: as heard, so the answer sounds like a word

annotation.surface: They say a cat thinks.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition describes the answer as a verb: a cat mews.
annotation.definitionFit: A cat mews, making its thin cry.

entries.clue: Adult on his travels? Very strange (10)

indicators.note: something that travels moves from place to place, so the letters change position

annotation.surface: A grown man abroad, finding everything odd.
annotation.walkthrough: 'On his travels' reads as one phrase; 'on his' is fodder and 'travels' the signal. OUTLANDISH also hints at foreign lands.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: outlandish once meant foreign, from an out-land, and now means bizarre or freakish.

entries.clue: Drink consumed after article pushed back (3)

indicators.note: the A is moved to the end

blocks.note: the indefinite article, the A at the front of ATE, which moves to the back

annotation.surface: A drink downed once an item was postponed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' looks like a separate piece to add; it is the A already at the front of ATE, which moves to the end.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: tea, brewed from dried leaves in hot water, is one kind of beverage.

entries.clue: Jeering exhausted amateurs in south polar region (9)

indicators.note: emptied of the middle, leaving only the outside letters
one thing sitting in another is surrounded by it, so AS goes inside

annotation.surface: Worn-out amateur explorers at the South Pole are mocked.
annotation.walkthrough: 'South polar region' suggests the Antarctic, but the polar region here is the northern one, with 'south' a separate letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: sarcastic talk is cutting and derisive, the tone of someone who taunts.

entries.clue: Seals experience narrow escape (5,5)

blocks.note: to have a good time = to experience it

annotation.surface: Marine mammals have a lucky escape.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Seals' looks like the animals; it is the verb. The wordplay splits one letter away from the enumeration's word space.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: a close shave is a near miss, from a razor passing within a whisker of cutting the skin.

entries.clue: Stoned, as one’s avocado might be (7)

blocks.note: slang for very drunk or high on drugs
avocado crushed onto toast, the fashionable brunch dish

annotation.surface: An avocado with its stone out, or a stoned diner, over brunch.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stoned' teases the avocado's stone; it means intoxicated, and so does SMASHED, which is also what brunch cafés do to avocado.
annotation.definitionFit: Smashed is slang for drunk or high, and smashed avocado is mashed.

entries.clue: Nobleman just about to lose case (4)

indicators.note: the outer letters, the word's casing, are removed

blocks.note: nearly = just about; drop N and Y

annotation.surface: A lord is on the point of losing a court action.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Case' reads as a lawsuit; here it is the outer shell of NEARLY.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: an earl is a British peer ranking above a viscount and below a marquess.

entries.clue: Try leaving hospital refuge sober (7)

indicators.note: someone leaving a place goes out of it, so H departs from the word

blocks.note: HEAR (try a case) without H for hospital

annotation.surface: An attempt to leave a hospital shelter for alcoholics while sober.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Try' is the judge's verb: to hear a case is to try it.
annotation.definitionFit: Earnest means serious and sober in manner.

entries.clue: A country once mostly forming large land area (4)

indicators.note: most of something is nearly all of it, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: SIAM, the old name of Thailand, without its M

annotation.surface: A former nation largely made up a great tract of territory.
annotation.walkthrough: SIAM is the old name for Thailand, a common crossword 'country once'. The answer is also the continent Siam belongs to.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Asia is a continent, the biggest of the seven, stretching from Turkey to Japan.

entries.clue: Design of steps announced (5)

indicators.note: spoken out, so the answer sounds like a word

blocks.note: a stile is a set of steps over a fence

annotation.surface: A staircase design is unveiled.
annotation.walkthrough: A stile is a set of steps for climbing over a fence or wall, common on British footpaths.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a style is the distinctive look or pattern of something made, as in a dress or house.

entries.clue: Miriam late up? It’s of no consequence (10)

indicators.note: stirred up, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Someone shrugs off Miriam getting up late.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Late up' reads as a lie-in; 'late' is fodder and 'up' the signal.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: something immaterial does not matter, being irrelevant or trivial to the point at issue.

entries.clue: Mum’s game over, start to relax (5)

indicators.note: the start of a word is where it begins, its opening letter

blocks.note: checkmate ends a game of chess

annotation.surface: Mother finishes her game and begins to unwind.
annotation.walkthrough: MATER is Latin for mother, used in dated British schoolboy slang.
annotation.definitionFit: Mater is a jokey or old-fashioned word for mother.

entries.clue: Line shared by neo-Marxists and anti-Semites? (6)

annotation.definition: Line shared by neo-Marxists and anti-Semites?

blocks.note: the surface reading: a party line, a position two camps might hold in common
the setter's reading: look at how the two words are printed, not what they mean

annotation.surface: Two opposed political camps agree on a party line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Line' suggests a political position; it is the little dash in 'neo-Marxists' and 'anti-Semites'.
annotation.definitionFit: A hyphen is a short line joining parts of a word.

entries.clue: Tryst with Eva turning into farce (8)

indicators.note: turning over, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A secret date with Eva descends into farce.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface has the farce happen; the definition is simply the noun farce.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a travesty is a grotesque parody or mockery, as in 'a travesty of justice'.

entries.clue: Demands of Treasury barely fell (3)

indicators.note: stripped bare, losing the outside letters

blocks.note: taxes are what the Treasury demands; drop T and S

annotation.surface: The Treasury's demands scarcely dropped.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like the past of fall; it is the verb to cut down a tree.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym, both verbs: lumberjacks chop down trees, and to cut one down with a blade is to axe it.

entries.clue: Increasingly sentimental tears regularly shed on boat (8)

indicators.note: every other letter is dropped
in an across clue, placed after

blocks.note: a tender is a small boat serving a larger one
tEaRs losing T, A and S

annotation.surface: Someone grows ever more emotional, shedding tears on a boat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tears shed' reads as crying; 'shed' works on the letters of 'tears'.
annotation.definitionFit: Tenderer is the comparative of tender, more sentimental.

entries.clue: Lead on clubs to eliminate onset of racism in full (6)

indicators.note: C comes in and puts the R out

blocks.note: C = clubs, the card suit, taking R's place

annotation.surface: Football clubs are pushed to stamp out racism completely.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Lead on clubs' reads as leading a card suit; 'Lead on' is the definition, meaning to tempt.
annotation.definitionFit: Idiom: to lead someone on is to tempt or lure them, often with false hopes.
